rounds.text: Mayur Uniquoters Ltd trades at a P/E of 15.2x, presenting a stark valuation discount against its sector benchmark of 25.75x [E1, E6]. This low multiple stands in sharp contrast to high-tier capital efficiency metrics, including a Return on Capital Employed of 24.5% and a Return on Equity of 18.0% [E12, E13]. Fundamental momentum is robust, evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth accelerating by 36% alongside a 16% rise in sales [E17, E21]. Operational strength is further reinforced by a fortress balance sheet carrying a near-zero debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and robust operating cash flows of Rs 133 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E38]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model projects an intrinsic value of Rs 1802 per share, yielding a 59.9% margin of safety against the current market price [E46, E47]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings declined to 3.13% as of June 2026 from 9.68% in September 2023 [E44].

The market is pricing in deceleration and structural risks that are visible across the operational and historical record. Earnings growth is explicitly flagged as decelerating by the rules-based screen [E66], and quarterly operating margins have turned inconsistent over the last two quarters [E33]. Furthermore, the polyurethanes business remains muted without successful volume or sales increases [E78], and footwear demand has suffered from drastic spikes in raw material and sole prices [E76]. Compounded share price growth over the long term has lagged significantly behind profit growth, standing at a mere 5% over 10 years [E22] compared to 9% profit growth [E18], and historical drawdowns have reached a severe peak-to-trough decline of -77.1% [E54]. Conceded: the company maintains a very low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and strong returns on capital employed [E10, E38]. Management itself highlights major headwinds including market volatility, Trump tariffs, and the West Asia war, which have delayed strategic decisions on international plant locations [E88] amid a broader global trend toward deglobalization [E90].

Conceded: the rules-based screen notes earnings growth deceleration [E66], and quarterly operating margins are inconsistent over the last two quarters [E33]. Conceded: the polyurethane business is currently muted [E78], footwear demand faced pressure from raw material and sole price spikes [E76], and the worst historical drawdown reached -77.1% [E54]. However, the bear's focus on a 10-year share price growth of 5% [E22] ignores the reality that fundamentals are currently outpacing long-term trends, with trailing twelve-month profit growth accelerating at 36% [E21] and 5-year profit growth reaching 17% [E19]. The bear's citation of management's macro concerns regarding tariffs and global volatility [E88] overlooks the concrete operational momentum of a newly ordered capacity expansion providing an additional 5 lakh meters [E79], which is projected to generate around ₹150 crores more per year annually [E86]. Furthermore, the long-term share price lag [E22] actually highlights a disconnect where strong financial execution—such as a 24.5% ROCE [E12] and pristine debt-to-equity of 0.01x [E38]—has not yet been fully reflected in valuations, as underscored by a conservative reverse DCF implying only 4.4% earnings growth is currently priced in [E48].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth is 36% [E21], 5-year profit growth is 17% [E19], ROCE is 24.5% [E12], and debt-to-equity is 0.01x [E38]. However, invoking these strong financials to dismiss long-term trends ignores the reality that 10-year compounded share price growth sits at a meager 5% [E22] and 5-year growth at only 9% [E23], demonstrating a persistent structural lag rather than a temporary disconnect. The bull relies on a reverse DCF implying 4.4% earnings growth [E48] and a projected capacity expansion of 5 lakh meters generating ₹150 crores [E79, E86], but glosses over the underlying vulnerabilities explicitly flagged by management, including severe raw material and sole price spikes that recently muted footwear demand [E76], a muted polyurethane business that has failed to drive volume or sales [E78], and acute pricing pressure where short-term cost increases impact the company until passed on [E89]. Moreover, pointing to operational momentum while ignoring management's own warnings about Trump tariffs, the West Asia war, and deglobalization [E88, E90]—which have paralyzed plant location decisions—highlights a volatile operating backdrop that threatens the realization of those projected gains. Finally, the automated rules-based screen explicitly confirms that earnings growth is decelerating [E66], directly contradicting the notion of unblemished forward momentum and justifying caution despite the backward-looking profitability metrics.

Conceded: 10-year compounded share price growth is 5% [E22] and 5-year share price growth is 9% [E23]. However, citing historical share price lag ignores the fundamental reality that profit growth is drastically outpacing share price performance over a 5-year horizon, directly signaling a valuation dislocation [E57]. The bear’s concern over footwear demand mutes and raw material volatility [E76, E82] overlooks management's confirmation that those pricing challenges are temporary before being successfully passed on to customers [E89], supported by an expanding operating margin that rose to 25% in the TTM from 20% three years prior [E30]. Conceded: the automated screen flags decelerating earnings growth [E66], but this is contradicted by live acceleration metrics showing TTM profit growth accelerating to 36% [E21] alongside robust 16% TTM sales growth [E17]. Furthermore, the paralysis in locating a new international plant due to macroeconomic headlines [E88, E90] is entirely neutralized by concrete, near-term domestic expansion: an ordered coating line and a 5-lakh-meter production line starting in early 2027 within existing facilities [E79, E81], which will deliver roughly ₹150 crores in annual potential [E86] without overseas execution risk.

Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 36% [E21] and operating margins expanded to 25% [E30]. However, pointing to this as a valuation dislocation ignores that historical compounded share price growth has limped along at a meager 5% over 10 years [E22] and 9% over 5 years [E23], demonstrating a persistent, long-term market reluctance to reward the underlying earnings with higher valuations. Furthermore, dismissing raw material volatility and footwear demand mutes as easily resolvable [E76, E82] contradicts management's own admissions that these shocks create immediate short-term impacts before price hikes can crawl through to customers [E89], leaving margins vulnerable to volatile petroleum by-product costs [E84]. While the bull celebrates avoiding overseas execution risk by shifting expansion to existing facilities [E79, E81], management itself remains paralyzed by deglobalization, Trump tariffs, and West Asia wars, explicitly citing these macroeconomic headwinds as roadblocks to establishing necessary international plants [E88, E90]. Finally, the automated screening engine explicitly flags decelerating earnings growth as a substantive risk [E66], indicating that relying solely on TTM spikes [E21] masks underlying cyclical volatility and a broader pattern of inconsistent quarterly margins [E33].

evidence.quote: So, we have said in the last phone call also, our expectation from domestic growth is between 8%-10%.

evidence.fact: Management expects export growth to range from 15% to 20%.
evidence.quote: And our expectation from export growth is from 15%-20%.

evidence.fact: The company targets a 15% growth rate in the coming year.
evidence.quote: So we have kept potential outlook for 15% growth in the coming year also.

evidence.fact: Footwear segment demand was muted in the last quarter due to drastic increases in raw material and sole prices.
evidence.quote: So specifically, our footwear business, because you have to understand the price of raw material for footwear, not only the PVC prices, the sole prices increased drastically to -- it went up to almost like 2x, 3x last year -- sorry, in the last quarter. So obviously, the market was muted in the footwear segment.

evidence.fact: Recent FTAs signed by India are viewed as a very positive move that will increase cost effectiveness and customer procurement sentiments from Europe.
evidence.quote: I think so it's a very positive move for India. Definitely, we will be more effective in terms of cost. The sentiments of the customers to procure from India will definitely increase. So and definitely both especially in the Europe market, I mean very good sentiments are coming.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the polyurethane business is still muted and has not succeeded much in volume or sales increases.
evidence.quote: So, PU, still the business is muted right now. We have not been able to succeed too much in terms of the volume in PU and increasing in sales.

evidence.fact: An additional production line has been ordered for current premises with production expected to start towards the end of February or March 2027.
evidence.quote: So we should be able to start our production by -- towards the end of this financial year, somewhere between February, March 2027. So we'll have an additional production capacity of 5 lakh meters.

evidence.fact: Management noted that international plant location options include Mexico, the US, or other NAFTA areas.
evidence.quote: So it could be in Mexico, it could be in U.S., it could be in some other NAFTA areas. We are still considering various options, but there's so much of volatility in the market.

evidence.fact: The company has ordered a coating line to be placed in an existing facility instead of putting it in South India.
evidence.quote: In India, we have ordered a coating line. But instead of putting it in South India, we have found space in an existing facility only. So, we will put it here. So, our capacity will increase.

evidence.fact: Raw material prices have experienced sharp volatility, rising, falling, and increasing again since March.
evidence.quote: The prices went up very sharply, then there was a fall in prices of some raw materials. Then again, the prices went up again. So, it's been a very volatile situation.

evidence.fact: A 10% natural hedge occurred on US dollar exports due to currency appreciation.
evidence.quote: Right? If today I was selling material for US$8 and I was having realization of 85 to 86, so at 94 I was getting a 10% natural hedge.

evidence.fact: Raw material prices for petroleum by-products like paste PVC went up significantly, but prices have softened a little bit from the highs of March.
evidence.quote: So, obviously, it's a petroleum by-product. So, the prices have gone up and the prices have gone up significantly. So, there was a challenge initially in the month of March where people were expecting that there could be an issue regarding the availability of the raw material. But I think those issues are resolved now. And prices have also softened a little bit from the highs of March.

evidence.fact: Current capacity utilization is running between 75% and 78%.
evidence.quote: So, we are utilizing somewhere between 75% to 78%.

evidence.fact: The upcoming capacity addition of 5 lakh meters will provide around 150 crores more per year annually based on average prices.
evidence.quote: So just simple, like if you just add 5 lakh meters into INR300 linear meter average price, so it will just give you the -- it's around INR150 crores more per year annually, then we have some capacity in an additional facility also.

evidence.fact: The company sold 31 million meters in volume for FY26, representing a volume growth of approximately 5%.
evidence.quote: 31 million meters.

evidence.fact: Management flagged market volatility, Trump tariffs, and West Asia war as reasons making it difficult to decide on exact plant locations.
evidence.quote: But because of all this Trump tariff, the West Asia war or multiple things happening in the last few years, we have not taken a final call where -- which should be the ideal location to put our plant.

evidence.fact: Management noted that short-term price increases impact the company until price hikes are passed on to customers.
evidence.quote: Because it takes some time to pass on the price increase to the customers. Definitely, it impacts a little bit in the short-term.

evidence.fact: Management notes the world is moving towards deglobalization as a consideration for evaluation.
evidence.quote: But world is moving towards deglobalization also. So as a counter measure, those things we are evaluating to put up a plant somewhere, not taking a final call there, but somewhere outside India definitely.

evidence.quote: And this sales growth and increased momentum is expected to continue in the next 2, 3 years.

evidence.quote: So we should be able to start our production by -- towards the end of this financial year, somewhere between February, March 2027.
